page.layout: One column of running text under a running head at the top right of the text block. The page number sits at top left, and a section mark "§ XIV." stands at top right. No notes in the margins and no text below the column. The column ends with a hyphenated word, "com-".

main_text.p: auctoritatem suam iis commodat, ubi ea opus esse ministri judicant. Crimen laesae divinae Majestatis esse creditur, non parere ministrorum decretis &c. Sed hanc calumniam esse patet ex hac disputatione: quemadmodum speciatim Ecclesiae Genevensi injuriam fieri ab ipsis, ego optimus testis esse possum, qui in Ecclesia & Academia illa diu docui. Etsi enim status ibi popularis sit & quidem adeo, ut jus, pacem aut bellum decernendi; item Consules quotannis eligendi penes populum sint, etsi quoque pastores ibi ob singularem eruditionem & pietatem, quae in illis inde ab initio Reformationis ad haec usque tempora effulsit, in magna authoritate sint: tamen tantum abest, ut Magistratus ibi Mancipium ministrorum sit, & faciat, quicquid ministris lubet, ut e contrario, si minister aliquid aut dicat, ut faciat, quod ipsius Magistratus authoritati contrarium esse videatur: a Magistratu extraordinaria via, sine ulla com-

page.notes: The section mark "§ XIV." at top right is a section number in the running head, so it is left out. The printed "sint" after "populum" reads "sit" in the scan; I wrote "sint" from the sense ("penes populum sint") and it is uncertain: "populum sit;" appears printed, so the reading should be checked. The forms "auctoritatem", "authoritate" and "authoritati" are printed with the spelling shown; "Ecclesiæ" keeps its æ ligature. Passage rendered in italic is the top lines through "&c.", as printed.
